quote: Okay. Y'all out and out sell panels?
stewart_read: Customer, despite declining upfront, asks an unprompted question about Ion's product directly — a sign of live curiosity the rep could use to keep the conversation open rather than answer flatly and move to a technical spec.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to treat unsolicited product questions as a hook — a brief curiosity-building reply ('Great question — that's actually part of why I wanted to grab a few details') keeps momentum instead of a flat factual answer.

quote: The panels we use, I believe that they are 440 watts.
stewart_read: Rep answers a technical spec question (panel wattage) directly instead of redirecting to the closer/specialist — minor scope creep, though brief and not escalating into a debate.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as simple rapport-building small talk rather than true scope creep since it's a single factual answer, not a sales pitch.
coaching_implication: Use the universal escape hatch here: 'That's exactly the kind of detail our specialist walks through once we look at your usage' instead of quoting spec numbers, which invites more technical questions the setter isn't equipped to answer (as happened immediately after).

quote: My electric bill used to be, like, $15.20 dollars, and to go from there to, like, 200 and something wasn't gonna happen.
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a striking bill-jump anchor unprompted — this is a stronger curiosity hook than most calls get, but no rep line in the transcript reflects it back, questions it, or uses it before she starts to withdraw two lines later.
alternative_hypothesis: It is possible a rep response occurred here but was misattributed to the customer track by the diarizer, given known unreliability in this transcript; however, no version of events in the transcript shows the bill being used, so the miss stands regardless of who said what next.
coaching_implication: Flag this as the single biggest missed opening on the call — a simple reflection ('That's a huge jump — did something change, or is this from your current system underperforming?') keeps her engaged instead of letting her drift toward 'I'll think about it.'

quote: I I I'll think about it and perhaps call back.
stewart_read: Customer begins to exit softly right after the unaddressed bill complaint; rep does pull her back with a next-step offer at 01:34, so this isn't a full miss, but it shows the cost of not flipping the bill pain immediately before.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may have sensed the DQ was coming (leased system) and chose not to over-invest emotional energy before confirming ownership — however the ownership question isn't asked until 02:03, after the recovery attempt, so this reads as reactive rather than a deliberate sequencing choice.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to resolve/acknowledge a stated pain point before it triggers a withdrawal, rather than recovering after the fact.

quote: So, yeah, you would be leasing it. And in that case, we actually are not able to help out. So I'll just take you off my list.
stewart_read: Clean, correct execution of the hard DQ once ownership structure (leased, no loan) is confirmed — no wasted time arguing or pushing past a disqualifying answer.
coaching_implication: This is a positive example to reinforce — the rep didn't over-invest once the disqualifying fact was on the table. Point to this as the model for closing out orphaned leads efficiently.
